newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka deports Swiss facing child abuse charges.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka deports Swiss facing child abuse charges.

text.p: Sri Lanka on Tuesday deported a Swiss national charged here with gross indecency and grave sexual abuse of children, police said.

Police said Viktor Baumann, from Zurich and a long-time resident of Sri Lanka, left on an Air Lanka flight. He is to stand trial in connection with several child sex charges in Sri Lanka, Thailand and other countries, police said.
"He is not going free. Swiss authorities are awaiting his arrival," Deputy Inspector General Mohamed Nizam told Reuters.

Baumann, 53, a foreign investor and a resident of Sri Lanka for the past eight years, was arrested last October in the company of several local children at his house near the coastal resort of Negombo, 24 miles (38 km) north of Colombo.
He was charged with gross indecency between persons and grave sexual abuse, Nizam said.
He was remanded for two weeks and released on bail. He was due to be indicted at a local court hearing on February 26.
Police decided to deport Baumann because of charges pending against him in other countries. Baumann will be tried for all the charges in Switzerland, Nizam said.
"In Switzerland he is wanted for sexual offences, we're unsure of the exact nature of his offences in other countries," he said.

In a separate case, Nizam said police have asked immigration authorities to deport Armin Heinrich Pfaffhauser, a 58-year-old Swiss national who last week was sentenced to two years in jail for "committing an unnatural offence" on two Sri Lankan boys.
Pfaffhauser is the first foreigner to be convicted of the offence. He pleaded not guilty.
"It is government policy that anyone who perpetrates crimes on children should not be tolerated on our shores," he said.
But children's rights organisations oppose plans to deport Pfaffhauser.
"Let him serve his sentence and then be deported," said Maureen Seneviratne of Protecting Environment and Children Everywhere (PEACE), a group trying to curb child sex tourism.
Child abuse cases are also pending against a German and a Belgian national in Sri Lankan courts. Another Swiss national, who jumped bail, is being tried in absentia.
Sri Lanka last year passed tough new laws aimed at curbing paedophile activity, said to be rampant along the tropical island's western coastal belt.
The new law calls for a minimum 10-year jail-term and a maximum 20-year sentence for pimps and their clients. It pushed the minimum age of consent up to 18 for boys and 16 for girls.
President Chandrika Kumaratunga last week ordered a nationwide crackdown on sexual abuse of children.
Kumaratunga set up a Child Protection Authority and asked a presidential panel to draw up an action plan to deal with sexual abuse of children.

The government has said it plans to make child abuse a non-bailable offence, create desks with specially trained women officers in all police stations and set up a telephone "help line" for the public to report offences.
